scope: Same-input isolated process comparisons on one macOS machine; no live App or live DB workload. First pass and targeted recheck are separate preserved experiments.

wall_anomaly.targeted_recheck: completed separately; does not replace this first-pass observation

query_assessment.memory_engineering_review: PASS: first-pass median reported peak RSS +245760 bytes (+0.015160%); recheck -40960 bytes (-0.002527%); packed capacity is exactly equal. This is not mathematical zero RSS growth.
query_assessment.paired_block_variation: All block values are retained per query; some individual blocks exceed +5% even though aggregate query/code/group medians pass.
query_assessment.query_external_sampler_identity_limit: RSS-only external samples do not record process startup cookies; child self-reported RSS/footprint and equal capacity provide the primary memory evidence.

measurement_limits: Query CPU/wall enclose search only; result encoding and diagnostic sampling are outside those timers. Group totals sum all three iterations within each process.

Query aggregate medians pool 12 baseline and 6 candidate observations per query in the first pass, and 18 baseline and 9 candidate observations in the recheck. Paired changes compare candidate to surrounding baseline medians within each block.

Query RSS sampler interval is 5 ms; footprint points are child self-reports after load and after result drop. Neither observes all transient peaks. Lifetime high-water RSS includes loading, searching and result serialization.
Upsert CPU/wall includes BEGIN, real production preparation/upsert, writer drop and COMMIT. Preload, input mutation, complete field equality, hashes and JSON are outside the phase timers.
Upsert memory includes the retained input vector and complete-field verification; 10 ms samples can miss peaks. Phase cumulative HWM is not phase-only allocation.

Upsert uses the same driver source; only the prepared_upsert compile flag changes use of the production caller API. Baseline outer-file write counts are unavailable; candidate counts are measured. No runtime total_changes counter is exposed.
Fresh indexed_at generations remain real writes and revision increments. These measurements do not justify suppressing generation updates.
DB/WAL size snapshots do not measure physical write bytes. APFS clones and repeated runs do not imply cold caches or independent physical storage.
Two first-pass blocks, three targeted recheck blocks and one upsert block describe this machine and input; they are not a statistical proof or real FSEvents delivery test.
GUI model-phase timing, native behavior, App installation and long-duration recovery are separate evidence and remain outside these query/upsert gates.
